title: Light, cells and the distance between them.
label: Evidence varies by outcome
deck: Red-light therapy is often discussed as if it were one treatment with one evidence level. It isn't. Wavelength, dose, target tissue, protocol and outcome all matter.

title: The skin barrier. The delivery question. The bigger claim.
label: Early human delivery research
deck: Glutaryl is Auro Wellness's topical glutathione spray. The manufacturer pairs glutathione with cyclodextrin in a skin-applied delivery system. This overview separates delivery research from broad health claims.

title: What the night leaves behind.
label: Human observational research
deck: A major 2026 Nature study linked sleep duration with biological-ageing clocks across multiple organs and molecular systems. The interesting part is not “sleep more.” It is the shape of the relationship.

title: One microbe. An entire ecosystem.
label: Preparation-specific human trials
deck: The excitement around Akkermansia muciniphila has moved from correlations into human trials. Here is what they can and cannot say.

title: An extraordinary claim needs an ordinary, repeatable test.
label: Supplier claims; clinical validation unresolved
deck: Leela sells products described using “quantum energy” and bioenergetic concepts. Youtopia's first job is not to dismiss or endorse them — it is to separate the claim, measurement and evidence.

title: The quiet infrastructure of a living body.
label: Animal mechanisms; selected human vascular research
deck: From capillary networks to nitric oxide: how blood vessels support the body, and what emerging research can actually tell us.

title: The enzyme, the promise and the missing outcome.
label: Mixed human trial findings
deck: A fermented-soy enzyme has become a biohacking favourite. The human evidence asks for more caution than the headlines allow.

title: Beyond the gym. Into a more difficult question.
label: Established exercise use; emerging cognitive research
deck: A well-studied training supplement has become a memory conversation. The evidence for these two uses is at different stages.

title: Broccoli, redesigned. What changes in the capsule?
label: Ingredient research; product claims require separate proof
deck: A broccoli-derived supplement raises a practical question: does a more stable capsule deliver the molecule, and does that translate into better health?

title: Water, wonder and the experiment in between.
label: Supplier hypothesis; health benefit unestablished
deck: Before looking at a price or checkout button, understand the idea. Aǹalemma markets a quartz wand designed to change the organisation of water through what it calls coherent water technology.

title: Small organisms. A much bigger nutrition story.
label: Food composition; selected short-term human trials
deck: Nutrition, cellular mechanisms and space-food research—follow the evidence behind the algae conversation.

title: NAD rises. What happens to the person?
label: Short human trials; long-term outcomes unresolved
deck: The most important question about nicotinamide mononucleotide is what happens after the biomarker moves.

title: The plunge. The response. The longer view.
label: Limited, outcome-dependent human evidence
deck: Cold-water immersion is everywhere. The evidence is more interesting — and more nuanced — than either the evangelists or the eye-rollers suggest.

title: When a familiar word feels further away.
label: Clinical assessment before supplement claims
deck: For the person who misplaces a word, forgets a name or feels less sharp: a useful first step is to understand what has changed, before shopping for a brain supplement.

title: A conversation between two worlds.
label: Human association; causality unresolved
deck: Researchers are bringing the gut–brain conversation into sharper focus by measuring microbial potential alongside chemistry in living human brains.

title: The clock is moving. What does it mean?
label: Multi-study analysis; surrogate outcomes unresolved
deck: A younger biological-age score makes a powerful headline. Understanding what moved, and why, makes a better story.

title: Reading biological time in a vial of blood.
label: Exploratory, disease-specific trial analysis
deck: Could a disease-focused trial reveal something about ageing too? Protein-based clocks offer a new way to ask.

title: A rare window into the living brain.
label: Selected human tissue research
deck: Understanding a disease while it unfolds can ask different questions from examining what remains afterwards.
